articles.headline: U.S. Designates Cyber-related and Transnational Criminal Organizations; Imposes New Cuba Sanctions
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new designations targeting cyber-related and transnational criminal organizations. This action aims to disrupt illicit activities that pose a threat to U.S. national security and financial stability.

Concurrently, OFAC also imposed new sanctions related to Cuba. These measures include a determination paving the way for sanctions on the electronics, manufacturing, marine, and technology sectors of the Cuban economy.
The new Cuba-related sanctions are part of an ongoing effort to pressure the Cuban government by targeting key economic sectors and individuals supporting the regime.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes New Iran-Related Designations, Amends Venezuela General License
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related designations and updated certain Iran-related listings. This action is part of the ongoing 'Operation Economic Outcast' by the Trump administration, which aims to cut off Iran's ability to sell oil and fund its military activities.

The Treasury also issued a new alert to industry, warning of sanctions risks associated with dealing with potentially false-flagged vessels. This comes as a Reuters investigation revealed a vast Iranian sanctions-evasion network involved in procuring military equipment.
Additionally, OFAC issued an amended Venezuela-related General License and a new Frequently Asked Question, indicating adjustments to existing sanctions policy concerning Venezuela.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues Amended Iran-Related General License
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has issued an amended Iran-related General License. This amendment signifies a modification to existing authorizations for certain transactions involving Iran.

The specific details of the amendment were not immediately disclosed in the brief announcement, but such changes typically aim to clarify or adjust the scope of permissible activities under the Iran sanctions program.
This action follows a period of heightened tensions and ongoing diplomatic efforts concerning Iran, with the U.S. continuing to utilize sanctions as a key policy tool.

articles.headline: OFAC Designates Entities Related to North Korea and Democratic Republic of the Congo
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new designations targeting entities related to North Korea and the Democratic Republic of the Congo. These actions are part of ongoing efforts to counter threats posed by these regions.
The North Korea designations likely target individuals or entities involved in the country's weapons of mass destruction programs or other illicit activities that generate revenue for the regime.
The Democratic Republic of the Congo-related designations aim to address issues such as human rights abuses, corruption, or destabilizing activities within the region.

articles.headline: OFAC Amends FAQs on Blocking, Rejecting Transactions, and Filing Reports
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has issued amended Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) regarding blocking and rejecting transactions and filing reports with OFAC. This update aims to provide clearer guidance to financial institutions and other entities on their compliance obligations.

The amendments likely address common questions and provide updated instructions on how to properly handle transactions involving sanctioned parties or jurisdictions, as well as the procedures for submitting required reports to OFAC.
These clarifications are crucial for ensuring effective implementation of U.S. sanctions programs and minimizing compliance risks for businesses operating internationally.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues Iran-Related, Russia-Related General Licenses; Removes Belarus and North Korea Designations
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related designations, alongside the issuance of new Iran-related and Russia-related General Licenses. This indicates a dynamic approach to sanctions policy, with both new restrictions and certain authorizations being introduced.

Notably, OFAC also announced the removal of certain designations related to Belarus and North Korea. This could signal a recalibration of sanctions pressure on these countries, potentially in response to specific developments or diplomatic considerations.
Additionally, amended Frequently Asked Questions were issued, likely providing further guidance on the scope and application of these new and modified sanctions measures.

articles.headline: OFAC Implements PAIPA Designations and Associated General Licenses
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has announced designations under the Protecting American Intellectual Property Act of 2022 (PAIPA). These designations are accompanied by the issuance of associated General Licenses.

PAIPA aims to protect American intellectual property by targeting individuals and entities involved in its theft or misappropriation. The new designations underscore the U.S. government's commitment to combating intellectual property theft globally.

The accompanying General Licenses are likely intended to mitigate any unintended consequences of the designations, allowing for certain transactions or activities that would otherwise be prohibited. The specific scope of these licenses will be crucial for affected parties.

articles.headline: OFAC Amends Venezuela-Related General License and FAQ
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has issued an amended Venezuela-related General License and a new Frequently Asked Question. This action indicates a continued adjustment of U.S. sanctions policy towards Venezuela.
The amendment to the General License likely modifies the scope of authorized transactions or activities involving Venezuela, potentially impacting various sectors or individuals.
The new FAQ aims to provide further clarity and guidance to the public regarding the application and interpretation of the Venezuela sanctions program.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes New Iran-Related and Cuba Designations, Issues New General Licenses
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related designations and a Cuba designation. These actions signify continued pressure on both countries through targeted sanctions.

In conjunction with these designations, OFAC also issued new and amended General Licenses and Frequently Asked Questions. These licenses and FAQs are crucial for understanding the permissible activities and compliance requirements under the updated sanctions regimes.
The designations and accompanying guidance reflect the U.S. government's ongoing strategy to address perceived threats and illicit activities associated with Iran and Cuba.

articles.headline: Extreme Networks, Inc. Settles with OFAC for $1,529,685
body: Extreme Networks, Inc. has reached a settlement agreement with the U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) for $1,529,685.

The settlement resolves nine apparent violations of the Ukraine-/Russia-Related Sanctions Regulations, 31 C.F.R. part 589. These violations stemmed from exports to a blocked Russian defense manufacturer between September 2018 and March 2022.
OFAC determined that the apparent violations were voluntarily self-disclosed by Extreme Networks, Inc. but were considered egregious.

articles.headline: Bank of America, N.A. Pays $11,662,930 in OFAC Civil Penalty
body: Bank of America, N.A. has paid a civil penalty of $11,662,930 to the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC).

This penalty is part of a larger coordinated enforcement action by the U.S. Treasury Department, which also included significant penalties from FinCEN and the OCC for anti-money laundering and sanctions failures.

OFAC's enforcement release cited 475 apparent violations totaling approximately $14.8 million, occurring from September 2021 to April 2025. These violations included payments sent to or through blocked banks and transactions involving designated individuals and other blocked parties across various sanctions programs, including Iran, Russia, narcotics, and global terrorism.

articles.headline: Fed Chair Warsh Warns Inflation Remains Too High, Pledges Action
body: U.S. Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh issued a warning that inflation remains excessively high, having consistently exceeded the central bank's 2% target for nearly six years. Speaking after the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting, Warsh reiterated the Fed's commitment to restoring price stability.

Warsh noted that while economic activity is expanding at a strong pace, driven by robust consumer spending and business investment, rising energy prices in recent weeks are a concern. He emphasized the need to prevent these sectoral price increases from broadening across the entire economy.

The Fed Chair stated that the FOMC's discussions primarily focused on curbing price pressures and pledged readiness to act as necessary. This suggests a continued hawkish stance from the Fed in its efforts to manage inflation.

articles.headline: Iran's Foreign Minister Holds Calls with Regional Powers Amid US Strike Fears
body: Iran's Foreign Minister has held calls with Oman, Qatar, and Saudi Arabia amidst fears of potential U.S. strikes. This diplomatic outreach follows reports of U.S. military strikes on Iranian targets in the Strait of Hormuz and the nearby mainland area of Bandar Abbas.

Iranian officials have celebrated the outcome of the U.S. midterm elections, viewing the Democratic gains as a rejection of President Trump's war policy. However, Iran is also bracing for potential further U.S. actions, including new strikes or a renewed push for a deal.
The ongoing tensions in the Middle East, now in their ninth month, have significantly impacted global energy prices and contributed to inflationary pressures worldwide.

articles.headline: South Korea to Expand Anti-Piracy Operations Closer to Strait of Hormuz
body: South Korea plans to extend its anti-piracy patrols, currently off the coast of Somalia, to waters closer to the Strait of Hormuz. This decision follows pressure from the United States to support operations related to the ongoing conflict with Iran.

The Ministry of National Defense will seek National Assembly approval to extend the mandate of the Cheonghae unit, a naval task force, and expand its operational area to include waters near the port of Duqm in Oman. Duqm is approximately 650km (403 miles) from the Strait of Hormuz.

Under the proposed new mandate, the unit's operating radius would roughly double to about 1,930km (1,200 miles), pushing northeast into the Arabian Sea south of Oman. The mission is described as strictly non-combat and will remain under South Korean command.

articles.headline: War of Attrition Takes Hold in Yemen One Month After Government Offensive
body: One month after Yemen's internationally recognized government launched a major offensive to reclaim Houthi-held territories, a war of attrition has taken hold. Analysts suggest that neither side shows signs of easing up, with both the Houthis and government forces, backed by a Saudi Arabia-led coalition, suffering and inflicting losses.

The offensive, dubbed 'Operation Dawn of Yemen,' aimed to retake control of all parts of the country held by the Houthis, including the capital Sanaa, which has been under Houthi control since late 2014.

Despite the government's claims of reclaiming control in certain areas, the conflict continues to exact a heavy toll on the civilian population, with reports of burning rubbish choking the besieged city of Taiz.

articles.headline: OCC Assesses Record $750 Million Penalty Against Bank of America for AML Failures
body: The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) has assessed a record $750 million civil money penalty against Bank of America, N.A. for its deficient and ineffective Bank Secrecy Act/Anti-Money Laundering (BSA/AML) compliance program.

This penalty is part of a coordinated enforcement action by the U.S. Department of the Treasury, which also included a $1.2 billion penalty from FinCEN and an $11.6 million settlement from OFAC. The OCC's action builds on a December 2024 cease-and-desist order against the bank.

Bank of America admitted to willfully violating the BSA by failing to maintain an adequate AML program, conduct due diligence on foreign correspondent accounts, and file Suspicious Activity Reports, resulting in the late reporting of over $5 billion in suspicious activity.

articles.headline: Streamlining Export Controls for Drone Exports
body: The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is easing export controls on certain Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs or drones) and related parts, components, accessories, attachments, technology, and software under the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). Specifically, this rule: eliminates wind gust tolerance as a parameter for determining UAV controls under the EAR; increases the threshold for national security controls on certain UAVs from an endurance of 30 minutes to an endurance of 3 hours; makes conforming changes to remove national security controls on software and technology associated with UAVs with an endurance less than 3 hours; maintains military end-use and end-user controls on those lower endurance drones and associated software and technology; clarifies Commerce Control List (CCL) controls for certain UAVs specially designed for military use; and removes national security controls on certain specially designed parts, components, accessories, and attachments for such UAVs as they do not provide any significant military or intelligence capabilities.

articles.headline: Implementation of EAR Export Controls on Silencers, Mufflers, and Sound Suppressors; and Other Firearms Related Changes
body: The Department of Commerce (Commerce), Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is revising the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) and the Commerce Control List (CCL) to appropriately control certain silencers, mufflers, and sound suppressors (sound suppressors) that will no longer be described on the International Traffic in Arms Regulations U.S. Munitions List (USML). This interim final rule (IFR) complements a Department of State interim final rule published elsewhere in this issue of the Federal Register (International Traffic in Arms Regulations: USML Category I Firearm Suppressors (1400-AG11) (State IFR)). This transfer of jurisdiction will reduce the regulatory burden on exports of sound suppressors. This IFR also revises the EAR to allow firearms and related items to be temporarily exported and reexported under a license exception as tools of trade, thereby relieving exporters of the regulatory burden of applying for authorization. Finally, this IFR clarifies which items fall within the scope of the EAR's entry clearance requirements for a temporary import.

articles.headline: Enhanced Favorable Treatment for the United Arab Emirates Under the Export Administration Regulations
body: In this final rule, the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) amends the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) to provide enhanced favorable treatment for the United Arab Emirates (UAE). Specifically, BIS is removing the UAE from Country Groups D:3 and D:4 and adding the UAE to Country Group A:5. More license exceptions will now be available, including Strategic Trade Authorization (STA) for the UAE Government and approved commercial entities in the UAE. STA will authorize the export, reexport, or transfer (in-country) of military items; certain commercial satellites and spacecraft; and dual-use items useful in, inter alia, oil and gas production, desalination, and civil nuclear power generation. The UAE Government and approved commercial entities will also have license-free access to advanced computing items, consistent with the May 2025 U.S.-UAE Artificial Intelligence Cooperation framework, without compromising U.S. digital infrastructure buildout.
